## Research question

A validator can miss semantic errors when judging a large generated SQL query as one unit without a trusted reference.

## Method

DecoVal enumerates restricted logical-plan rewrites and cuts them into blocks that recompose to the candidate. DP or A* minimizes a modeled validation cost using structural complexity, interface load, LLM-rated semantics and judgment count. LLMs write requirements and input descriptions; accepting every block accepts the query.

## Evaluation

Twenty SQL-proficient volunteers assess two clarified BEAVER tasks; analysis retains 17 judgments per presentation condition. Three LLM validators evaluate 305 generated candidates from support-filtered BEAVER/Spider 2.0 questions, labeled by benchmark execution evaluators. Baselines include repeated whole-query judgments, syntactic/random decompositions and round-trip or synthetic-execution validation.

## What the results support

Humans correctly reject in 10/11 judgments of erroneous candidates with decomposition versus 4/11 without, but median time on erroneous queries increases from 486 to 931 seconds. Default LLM error recall rises from 25.1% to 39.9% while false rejections increase from six to eight. Finer decomposition further trades specificity for recall.

## Limits and qualifications

Optimization is exact only within the enumerated space and chosen model; its probability interpretation assumes independent errors and valid per-task probabilities. Intent soundness additionally requires consistent requirements and correct local judgments. Requirements remain LLM-generated, thresholds are manually chosen, and benchmark execution labels are not semantic proofs. Five unsupported candidates receive no verdict but remain in metric denominators.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adjacent support for reference-free verification and human error localization under a fixed interpretation, not an evaluated ambiguity-resolution or unanswerability policy.
